# Upgrade TufinOS 3 to 4: In-place, VMWare ESXi, Central/Remote Collector Cluster, TOS Reinstall

## Overview

This procedure is for upgrading TufinOS 3 to 4 on the same VMWare ESXi machines in a central or remote collector cluster. For central clusters, this is relevant when there are changes to the server configuration. This requires upgrading first the worker nodes and then the data node.

If you have both central and remote collector clusters, upgrade the central cluster first.

During the TufinOS upgrade there will be some downtime. TOS will need to be reinstalled

## Is this the right procedure?

This procedure is ONLY for:

- TOS TOS 5

- Single data node remote collector clusters

- Single data node central clusters - if you plan on making changes to the server configurations (for example: IP address, server timezone)

- Upgrades on the same VMWare ESXI machines

If your TOS release is not TOS 5, go to the Knowledge Center that matches your TOS version. If other requirements are not met, [select a different procedure](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/ST2/TufinOS/UpgradingTufinOS3to4_VM.htm).

## Prerequisites

1. This procedure must be performed by an experienced Linux administrator with knowledge of network and storage configuration.

2. Ensure that each partition has at least 30% available space. No partition should exceed 70% usage.

   ```
   [<ADMIN> ~]$ df -h | awk '$5+0 > 70 {print $0}'
   ```

   Do not proceed with the upgrade until the output returns 0 results.

3. The rpcbind service is disabled by default when updating to this version, preventing NFS 3 from working. However, it can be enabled by running the following commands in sequence:

   ```
   systemctl unmask rpcbind.socket rpcbind.service
   ```

   ```
   systemctl start rpcbind.socket rpcbind.service
   ```

   ```
   systemctl enable rpcbind.socket rpcbind.service
   ```

4. **For data nodes only.** If you have not already separated the etcd database, add a second disk to the machine.

   - Size: 50 GB

   - Select a **storage type** of SSD. Take into consideration that TOS requires 7,500 IOPS and the throughput expected will average 250MB/s with bursts of up to 700MB/s.

## Downloads

1. Download the TufinOS 4.60 installation package from the [Download Center](https://portal.tufin.com/s/download-center?Product__c=TufinOS&Major_Version__c=4.60) to your local machine.

   - For a VMWare ESXi machine, download the .iso image file.

2. Extract the TufinOS image from its archive.

   ```
   [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo tar xzvf <FILENAME>.tgz
   ```

   The run file name includes the release, version, build number, and type of installation.

   TufinOS ISO file example: `TufinOS-4.60-4368238-x86_64-Final.iso`

3. Verify the integrity of the TufinOS installation package.

   ```
   [<ADMIN> ~]# sha256sum -c TufinOS-X.XX-XXXXXX-x86_64-Final.iso.sha256
   ```

   The output should return **OK**

## Preliminary preparations

1. <details>
   <summary>Verify that your deployment is compatible with TufinOS 4.60.</summary>

   1. Check your current TufinOS version:

      ```
      cat /etc/tufinos-release
      ```

      Your TufinOS release appears in the output. If the command is not recognized, you have a non-TufinOS operating system and cannot upgrade using this procedure.

   2. Review the [TufinOS 4 release history](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/ReleaseNotes/Common_RN_TOS/UpgradeTufinOS4.htm) and verify that you can perform the procedure.

   </details>

2. <details>
   <summary>Run the TOS precheck.</summary>

   **TOS precheck** assesses the health of your TOS environment, identifying potential issues that can impact your TufinOS upgrade.

   This procedure must be performed at least one week before you upgrade. Run **TOS precheck** to check for any misconfigurations that might interfere with the success of the upgrade, and send the output to Tufin Support for assessment. Do not begin the procedure until Tufin Support sends a confirmation.

   1. Run the TOS precheck:

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ ark tos-precheck
      ```

      The TOS precheck creates an output file - `/tmp/tos_check/tsc-[HOSTNAME]-[DATETIME].tgz`

   2. Download the output file to your personal computer.

   3. In the [Tufin portal](https://portal.tufin.com/s/system-evaluation), go to **Support Center** &gt; **System Evaluation**.

   4. In the **Upload the TOS Precheck output** section, upload the output file, and click **Submit for Analysis**.

      Only a single file can be uploaded. If you have multiple files, use Tar or Zip to compress them into a single file.

   5. Select the TOS release version you currently have installed.

   6. Click **Submit for Analysis**.

      An SR will be automatically opened and Tufin Support Engineers will contact you.

   7. Do not proceed with the upgrade until you receive confirmation from Tufin Support.

   </details>

3. <details>
   <summary>Check the cluster health.</summary>

   1. On the primary data node, check the following status.

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo systemctl status k3s
      ```

      Example output:

4. <details>
   <summary>Backup your TOS data. This needs to be performed for all primary data nodes - the central cluster and remote collector clusters.</summary>

   If you are going to perform this procedure over multiple maintenance periods, create a new backup each time.

   1. Create the backup using `tos backup create`:

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo tos backup create
      ```

      Example output:

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo tos backup create
      [Aug 23 16:18:42]  INFO Running backup
      Backup status can be monitored with "tos backup status"
      ```

   2. You can check the backup creation status using `tos backup status`, which shows the status of backups in progress. Wait until completion before continuing.

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo tos backup status
      ```

      Example output:

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo tos backup status
      Found active backup "23-august-2021-16-18"
      ```

   3. Run the following command to display the list of backups saved on the node:

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo tos backup list
      ```

      Example output:

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo tos backup list
      ["23-august-2021-16-18"]
      Started: "2025-12-23 13:18:43 +0000 UTC"
      Completed: "N/A"
      Modules: "ST, SC"
      HA mode: "false"
      TOS release: "25.2 (PGA.0.0) Final"
      TOS build: "21.2.2100-210722164631509"
      Expiration Date: "2021-09-22 13:18:43 +0000 UTC"
      Status: "Completed"
      ```

   4. Check that your backup file appears in the list, and that the status is **"Completed"**.

   5. If your backup files are saved [locally](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/ST2/ManagingTOS/CLI.htm#tosbackupstorageset):

      1. Run [sudo tos backup export](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/ST2/ManagingTOS/CLI.htm#tosbackupexport) to save your backup file from a TOS backup directory as a single `.gzip` file. If there are other backups present, they will be included as well.

      2. Transfer the exported `.gzip` file to a safe, remote location.

         Make sure you have the location of your backups safely documented and accessible, including credentials needed to access them, for recovery when needed.

      After the backup is exported, we recommend verifying that the file contents can be viewed by running the following command:

      ```
      [Target location]$ tar tzvf <filename>
      ```

   </details>

5. <details>
   <summary>Stop TOS.</summary>

   1. Run the command:

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo tos stop
      ```

      This process may take time.

   2. Check that all processes have been stopped successfully. Run the command:

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ watch -n 1 kubectl get pods
      ```

      A list of all pods is displayed.

      ##### Example

      ![Kubernetes kubectl get pods][img-kubernetes-kubectl-get-pods]

   3. Wait until all the pods, with the exception of the service controller, ps-proxy, and reportpack pods, have disappeared from the list or reached a status of **Completed**. The service controller, ps-proxy, and reportpack pods which can continue running.

      All TOS processes are now stopped on all the data nodes in the cluster.

   </details>

6. <details>
   <summary><b>Remote Collector clusters.</b> If you are currently upgrading the central cluster, make sure all the Remote Collector clusters are connected.</summary>

   On the Central cluster primary data node run:

   ```
   [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo tos cluster list
   ```

   The output shows all connected clusters.

   Example output:

   ```
   $ sudo tos cluster list
   NAME    ID    IP                TYPE

   Central    1                    master
   RC1        2    192.168.75.156    data_collector
   ```

   </details>

7. If you are running a multi-node cluster, get a list of your nodes.

   ```
   [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo tos cluster node list
   ```

8. <details>
   <summary>Save your TufinOS Configuration (repeat this step for each node).</summary>

   The TOS backup does not include your TufinOS configurations. Therefore, before you start create a list of the data you want to keep and save it outside the machine you are upgrading.

   After the upgrade completion, re-configure all your backed-up data before restoring TOS.

   For more information on what to information to save, see [Save Your TufinOS Configuration](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/ST2/TufinOS/data-to-backup.htm):

   > **Note:** If you have any questions about the upgrade, contact the Tufin support team. Do not attempt the upgrade if you are unsure about any part of it.

   </details>

## Upgrade worker nodes

Repeat these steps for each worker node.

1. <details>
   <summary>Remove the node from the cluster</summary>

   1. Identify the worker node you want to remove.

   2. <details>
      <summary>On the primary data node, check the status of the node you want to remove.</summary>

      Run [sudo tos cluster node list](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/ST2/ManagingTOS/CLI.htm#clusternodelist).

      </details>

      - If the node is in a healthy state:

        1. On the primary data node, run:

           ```
           [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo tos cluster node remove <node>
           ```

           #### Parameters

           | Parameter | Description | Required/Optional |
           |---|---|---|
           | `<node>` | Hostname of the node to remove. | Required |

           On completion, a new command string appears, which you will need to run on the node you want to remove within 30 minutes. If the allocated time expires, you will need to repeat the current step.

        2. Log in to the CLI of the node to be removed.

        3. On the node to be removed, run the command string displayed on completion of the command above. On completion, all TOS-related directories and data will be deleted from the node, therefore make sure you run it on the correct node. Running the command on the wrong node will destroy the cluster.

        All TOS-related directories will be deleted from the node.

      - If the node you want to remove is not in a healthy state:

        1. On the primary data node, run:

           ```
           [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo tos cluster node remove <node> --force
           ```

           #### Parameters

           | Parameter | Description | Required/Optional |
           |---|---|---|
           | `<node>` | Hostname address of the node to remove. | Required |

   3. Verify that the node has been removed by again running [sudo tos cluster node list](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/ST2/ManagingTOS/CLI.htm#clusternodelist).

   </details>

2. <details>
   <summary>Install TufinOS</summary>

   1. Place the TufinOS ISO image file on the datastore of vSphere. For local installation on a VMware machine, locate the extracted ISO image file.

   2. Confirm that in your virtual machine settings, **Boot Options** is configured to use BIOS. If you are using EFI, the procedure will not work.

   3. Edit the properties of the virtual CD/DVD drive, and do one of the following:

      Using vSphere:

      - As Device Type select **Datastore ISO file**, and browse to the TufinOS ISO image.

      - Under **Device Status**, select **Connect at power on**.

      Using a workstation:

      - Under **Device Status**, select **Connect at power on**.

      - Under **Connection**, select **Use ISO image file**, and browse to the TufinOS ISO image.

   4. Set the VM to boot to BIOS configuration.

      <details>
      <summary>Example using vSphere</summary>

      1. Navigate to **VM settings** &gt; **VM options**.

      2. Check: **During the next boot, force entry into the BIOS setup screen**.

         ![vm setting bios force entry][img-vm-setting-bios-force-entry]

      </details>

   5. In **BIOS** &gt; **Boot**, select **CD-ROM Drive**.

      ![bios boot cd][img-bios-boot-cd]

   6. In **BIOS** &gt; **Exit**, select **Exit Saving Changes**. Click **Yes**.

      ![bios exit saving changes][img-bios-exit-saving-changes]

   7. Save the settings.

   8. Restart the VM. TufinOS installation begins.

   9. Select **TufinOS 4.60 Installation for TOS Aurora**.

   10. Select **Install TufinOS 4.60 for Worker Node**.

   11. When prompted, confirm and choose **Yes**.

   12. When the installation is complete, reboot the virtual machine.

   13. When BIOS launches, change the Boot option to **Hard Drive**.

       ![bios boot hard drive][img-bios-boot-hard-drive]

   14. In **BIOS** &gt; **Exit**, select **Exit Saving Changes**. Click **Yes**.

       ![bios exit saving changes][img-bios-exit-saving-changes]

   15. Log in using the default admin user credentials:

       username: `tufin-admin`

       password: `admin` (you will be prompted to change this on first log in)

       IP address: assigned by DHCP

   </details>

3. <details>
   <summary>Set up the node.</summary>

   1. Give the node a unique name in the cluster

   2. Restore the TufinOS configuration data that you saved before beginning the upgrade procedure (see [Save Your TufinOS Configuration](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/ST2/TufinOS/data-to-backup.htm#Recommen)). In general we recommend that the new server configurations be similar to the old configurations.

   3. If you want to reset the host name or IP of the machine, do so now. It cannot be done at a later stage. See [Changing IP Address/Host Names](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/ST2/ManagingTOS/ChangingIPAddress.htm).

   4. If you want to configure NIC bonding, do so now. It cannot be done at a later stage. See [Link Redundancy on Tufin Appliances](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/ST2/TufinOS/nic-bonding.htm).

   5. Configure the server timezone.

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo timedatectl set-timezone <timezone>
      ```

      where `<timezone>` is in the format Area/Location. Examples: America/Jamaica, Hongkong, GMT, Europe/Prague.

      To view a list of the time-zone formats that can be used, run:

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo timedatectl list-timezones
      ```

      > **Note:** Ukraine only. Since the [change in timezone name from Kiev to Kyiv](https://mm.icann.org/pipermail/tz/2021-January/029679.html), not all software products have been adjusted. We therefore recommend avoiding these names and instead using an alternative city in the same timezone such as Europe/Tallinn.

   6. Synchronize your machine time with a trusted NTP server. Follow the steps in [Configuring NTP Using Chrony](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/Suite/chrony.htm). In an HA deployment, all servers need to be synchronized to the same time.

   7. Configure the IP address and DNS, where `<Interface Name>` is the name of the interface you are using (for example, ens32). If you have several network interfaces, configure the first one.

      <details>
      <summary>To find the first network interface</summary>

      Run the command:

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo /opt/tufinos/scripts/network_interface_by_pci_order.sh | awk -F'=' '/NET_IFS\[0\]/ { print $NF }'
      ```

      </details>

   8. To assign a static IP address or restore one that was used before upgrading:

      1. Run the command:

         ```
         [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo nmtui edit <Interface Name>
         ```

         ![EditConnection][img-editconnection]

         and set the following parameters in the window:

         - Set IPv4 CONFIGURATION to Manual

         - Set Addresses for the physical IP, together with the chosen subnet

         - Set Gateway and DNS Servers to the IPs used by your organization

      2. Restart the network service.

         ```
         [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo systemctl restart NetworkManager.service
         ```

   9. <details>
      <summary>Verify that the DNS server can resolve its own address using a reverse lookup</summary>

      Run:

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo nslookup <DNS SERVER IP>
      ```

      If the name of the server appears, the DNS server can resolve its own address using a reverse lookup.

      Example Output

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo nslookup  1.2.3.4
      4.3.2.1.in-addr.arpa	name=EXAMPLE.company.com
      ```

      If the name of the server does not appear, set it using a reverse lookup entry at /etc/hosts.

      Example Output where  `1.2.3.4 4.3.2.1.in-addr-arpa` was added.

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo cat /etc/hosts
      127.0.0.1 localhost localhost.localdomain localhost4 localhost4.localdomain4
      ::1 localhost6 localhost6.localdomain6
      1.2.3.4 admin.company.com admin
      2.3.4.5 5.4.3.2.in-addr-arpa
      ```

      </details>

   </details>

4. <details>
   <summary>Add the worker node back to the cluster.</summary>

   1. On the primary data node run:

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo tos cluster node add --role=<TYPE>
      ```

      where `<TYPE>` is worker or data, depending on the type of node you want to add.

      On completion, a new command string appears, which you will need to run on the new node within one hour. If the allocated time expires, you will need to repeat the current step.

   2. Log in to the CLI of the server to be added as a new node in the cluster.

   3. On the new node, run the command string displayed previously on the primary data node in step 2 above. If the allocated time has expired, you will need to start from the beginning.

   4. Verify that the node was added by running [sudo tos cluster node list](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/ST2/ManagingTOS/CLI.htm#clusternodelist) on the primary data node.

   </details>

5. <details>
   <summary>Check the cluster status.</summary>

   1. On the primary data node, check the TOS status.

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo tos status
      ```

   2. In the output, check if the `System Status` is `Ok` and all the items listed under `Components` appear as `Ok`. If this is not the case, contact Tufin Support.

## Upgrade the data node

1. <details>
   <summary>Backup your TOS data. This needs to be performed for all primary data nodes - the central cluster and remote collector clusters.</summary>

   If you are going to perform this procedure over multiple maintenance periods, create a new backup each time.

   1. Create the backup using `tos backup create`:

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo tos backup create
      ```

      Example output:

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo tos backup create
      [Aug 23 16:18:42]  INFO Running backup
      Backup status can be monitored with "tos backup status"
      ```

   2. You can check the backup creation status using `tos backup status`, which shows the status of backups in progress. Wait until completion before continuing.

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo tos backup status
      ```

      Example output:

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo tos backup status
      Found active backup "23-august-2021-16-18"
      ```

   3. Run the following command to display the list of backups saved on the node:

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo tos backup list
      ```

      Example output:

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo tos backup list
      ["23-august-2021-16-18"]
      Started: "2025-12-23 13:18:43 +0000 UTC"
      Completed: "N/A"
      Modules: "ST, SC"
      HA mode: "false"
      TOS release: "25.2 (PGA.0.0) Final"
      TOS build: "21.2.2100-210722164631509"
      Expiration Date: "2021-09-22 13:18:43 +0000 UTC"
      Status: "Completed"
      ```

   4. Check that your backup file appears in the list, and that the status is **"Completed"**.

   5. If your backup files are saved [locally](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/ST2/ManagingTOS/CLI.htm#tosbackupstorageset):

      1. Run [sudo tos backup export](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/ST2/ManagingTOS/CLI.htm#tosbackupexport) to save your backup file from a TOS backup directory as a single `.gzip` file. If there are other backups present, they will be included as well.

      2. Transfer the exported `.gzip` file to a safe, remote location.

         Make sure you have the location of your backups safely documented and accessible, including credentials needed to access them, for recovery when needed.

      After the backup is exported, we recommend verifying that the file contents can be viewed by running the following command:

      ```
      [Target location]$ tar tzvf <filename>
      ```

   </details>

2. <details>
   <summary>Upgrade TufinOS</summary>

   1. Place the TufinOS ISO image file on the datastore of vSphere. For local installation on a VMware machine, locate the extracted ISO image file.

   2. Confirm that in your virtual machine settings, **Boot Options** is configured to use BIOS. If you are using EFI, the procedure will not work.

   3. Edit the properties of the virtual CD/DVD drive, and do one of the following:

      Using vSphere:

      - As Device Type select **Datastore ISO file**, and browse to the TufinOS ISO image.

      - Under **Device Status**, select **Connect at power on**.

      Using a workstation:

      - Under **Device Status**, select **Connect at power on**.

      - Under **Connection**, select **Use ISO image file**, and browse to the TufinOS ISO image.

   4. Set the VM to boot to BIOS configuration.

      <details>
      <summary>Example using vSphere</summary>

      1. Navigate to **VM settings** &gt; **VM options**.

      2. Check: **During the next boot, force entry into the BIOS setup screen**.

         ![vm setting bios force entry][img-vm-setting-bios-force-entry]

      </details>

   5. In **BIOS** &gt; **Boot**, select **CD-ROM Drive**.

      ![bios boot cd][img-bios-boot-cd]

   6. In **BIOS** &gt; **Exit**, select **Exit Saving Changes**. Click **Yes**.

      ![bios exit saving changes][img-bios-exit-saving-changes]

   7. Save the settings.

   8. Restart the VM. TufinOS installation begins.

   9. Select **TufinOS 4.60 installation for TOS Aurora**.

   10. Select **Install TufinOS 4.60 for Data Node**.

   11. When prompted, confirm and choose **Yes**.

   12. When the installation is complete, reboot the virtual machine.

   13. When BIOS launches, change the Boot option to **Hard Drive**.

       ![bios boot hard drive][img-bios-boot-hard-drive]

   14. In **BIOS** &gt; **Exit**, select **Exit Saving Changes**. Click **Yes**.

       ![bios exit saving changes][img-bios-exit-saving-changes]

   15. Log in using the default admin user credentials:

       username: `tufin-admin`

       password: `admin` (you will be prompted to change this on first log in)

       IP address: assigned by DHCP

   </details>

3. <details>
   <summary>Set up the node.</summary>

   1. Give the node a unique name in the cluster

   2. Restore the TufinOS configuration data that you saved before beginning the upgrade procedure (see [Save Your TufinOS Configuration](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/ST2/TufinOS/data-to-backup.htm#Recommen)). In general we recommend that the new server configurations be similar to the old configurations.

   3. If you want to reset the host name or IP of the machine, do so now. It cannot be done at a later stage. See [Changing IP Address/Host Names](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/ST2/ManagingTOS/ChangingIPAddress.htm).

   4. If you want to configure NIC bonding, do so now. It cannot be done at a later stage. See [Link Redundancy on Tufin Appliances](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/ST2/TufinOS/nic-bonding.htm).

   5. Configure the server timezone.

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo timedatectl set-timezone <timezone>
      ```

      where `<timezone>` is in the format Area/Location. Examples: America/Jamaica, Hongkong, GMT, Europe/Prague.

      To view a list of the time-zone formats that can be used, run:

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo timedatectl list-timezones
      ```

      > **Note:** Ukraine only. Since the [change in timezone name from Kiev to Kyiv](https://mm.icann.org/pipermail/tz/2021-January/029679.html), not all software products have been adjusted. We therefore recommend avoiding these names and instead using an alternative city in the same timezone such as Europe/Tallinn.

   6. Synchronize your machine time with a trusted NTP server. Follow the steps in [Configuring NTP Using Chrony](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/Suite/chrony.htm). In an HA deployment, all servers need to be synchronized to the same time.

   7. Configure the IP address and DNS, where `<Interface Name>` is the name of the interface you are using (for example, ens32). If you have several network interfaces, configure the first one.

      <details>
      <summary>To find the first network interface</summary>

      Run the command:

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo /opt/tufinos/scripts/network_interface_by_pci_order.sh | awk -F'=' '/NET_IFS\[0\]/ { print $NF }'
      ```

      </details>

   8. To assign a static IP address or restore one that was used before upgrading:

      1. Run the command:

         ```
         [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo nmtui edit <Interface Name>
         ```

         ![EditConnection][img-editconnection]

         and set the following parameters in the window:

         - Set IPv4 CONFIGURATION to Manual

         - Set Addresses for the physical IP, together with the chosen subnet

         - Set Gateway and DNS Servers to the IPs used by your organization

      2. Restart the network service.

         ```
         [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo systemctl restart NetworkManager.service
         ```

   9. <details>
      <summary>Verify that the DNS server can resolve its own address using a reverse lookup</summary>

      Run:

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo nslookup <DNS SERVER IP>
      ```

      If the name of the server appears, the DNS server can resolve its own address using a reverse lookup.

      Example Output

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo nslookup  1.2.3.4
      4.3.2.1.in-addr.arpa	name=EXAMPLE.company.com
      ```

      If the name of the server does not appear, set it using a reverse lookup entry at /etc/hosts.

      Example Output where  `1.2.3.4 4.3.2.1.in-addr-arpa` was added.

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo cat /etc/hosts
      127.0.0.1 localhost localhost.localdomain localhost4 localhost4.localdomain4
      ::1 localhost6 localhost6.localdomain6
      1.2.3.4 admin.company.com admin
      2.3.4.5 5.4.3.2.in-addr-arpa
      ```

      </details>

   </details>

4. <details>
   <summary>Download TOS</summary>

   1. Run the [tmux command.](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/ST2/ManagingTOS/tmuxCommand.htm)

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ tmux new-session -s tosinstall
      ```

   2. Create the directory `/opt/misc/`, if it does not exist already.

   3. Go to `/opt/misc/`.

   4. Go to the [Download Center](https://portal.tufin.com/s/download-center?Product__c=TOS&Major_Version__c=5.4.00) and select the TOS 5.4.00 package.

   5. Select either **Download to Computer** or **Copy link (valid for 10m)**.

   6. If you selected copy link, run the following command within ten minutes:

      ```
      curl -o [Name the file].run.gz  "<LINK>"
      ```

      Where &lt;`LINK`&gt; is the link you copied from the Download Center.

      Make sure the server can download from `https://tosportaldownloads.tufin.com`.

   7. If you downloaded to the computer, upload the compressed file from your local computer to the server.

   8. Verify the integrity of the TOS installation packages by entering the following commands and comparing the output with the [checksum information](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/ReleaseNotes/tos5/AdditionalInfo.htm).

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sha256sum tos-xxxx-xxxxxxxx-final-xxxx.run.tgz
      ```

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sha1sum tos-xxxx-xxxxxxxx-final-xxxx.run.tgz
      ```

   9. Extract the TOS run file from its archive.

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ tar xvzf tos-xxxx-xxxxxxxx-final-xxxx.run.tgz
      ```

      The run file name includes the release, version, and build number.

      TOS file example: `tos_6.1.00-final-38281.run`

   </details>

5. <details>
   <summary>Reinstall TOS</summary>

   1. Run the TOS run file.

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ cd /opt/misc/
      ```

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo sh <runfile>
      ```

   2. Run the install command, replacing the parameters:

      - `<PRIMARY>`

      - `<SERVICE-CIDR>` - The CIDR you will use for the Kubernetes service network.

      - `<PODS-CIDR>` **Optional.** The CIDR you will use for the Kubernetes pods network. The default pods network is 10.244.0.0/16

      - `<MODULE-TYPE>` - One of the following values:

        - **ST** for SecureTrack only

        - **ST**, **SC** for both SecureTrack and SecureChange/SecureApp

        - **RC** for a remote collector

      - `<LOAD>` - small, medium or large, as provided by your account team, based on your sizing calculation.

      There is also an option to do a dry run, to verify the procedure in advance by going through all the stages without installing anything. To do a dry run, add the parameter `--dry-run` to the install command.

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]$ sudo tos install --modules=<MODULE-TYPE> --primary-vip=<PRIMARY> --services-network=<SERVICE-CIDR> --pod-network=<PODS-CIDR> --load-model=<LOAD> -d
      ```

      Examples:

      $ sudo tos install --modules=RC --primary-vip=162.148.10.0 --services-network=10.10.10.0/24 --load-model=large -d

   3. The EULA appears. After reading, enter `q` to exit the document. If you accept the EULA, enter `y` and wait until the command completes.

      ![CLI ST SC install][img-cli-st-sc-install]

   1. You can now safely exit the CLI tmux session:

      ```
      [<ADMIN> ~]# exit
      ```

   2. If the installation was for a central (main) cluster, log into TOS at https://&lt;VIP&gt; in your browser with user=admin, password=admin. If a warning message is shown regarding the site security certificate, 'accept the risk' and continue to the site. You will be prompted to set a new password.

      If the installation was for a remote collector, [connect it to the central cluster](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/ST2/ManagingTOS/RemoteCollectors.htm#connectrc).

   </details>

6. <details>
   <summary>Restore TOS</summary>

   If you are restoring from external storage:

   1. Connect to the external backup storage using [sudo tos backup storage set](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/ST2/ManagingTOS/CLI.htm#tosbackupstorageset). with the `<LOCATION>` as `external`.

   2. Run [sudo tos backup list](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/ST2/ManagingTOS/CLI.htm#tosbackuplist) to list all the backups and identify the one that you want to restore.

   3. Run [sudo tos restore](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/ST2/ManagingTOS/CLI.htm#tosrestore) specifying the desired backup. We recommend that you select the most recent backup. On completion, your data will have been restored.

   4. [Reinstall](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/Suite/Licenses_Add.htm) your license file.

   If you are restoring from a backup that was saved locally and transferred to a safe, external location:

   1. Copy the export file (`gzip` format) from the remote location to your primary data node.

   2. Run [sudo tos backup import](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/ST2/ManagingTOS/CLI.htm#tosbackupimport), specifying the full path of the export file, to extract all the backups from the export file to the TOS backup directory.

   3. Run [sudo tos backup list](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/ST2/ManagingTOS/CLI.htm#tosbackuplist) to list all the backups and identify the one that you want to restore.

   4. Run [sudo tos restore](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/ST2/ManagingTOS/CLI.htm#tosrestore) specifying the desired backup. We recommend that you select the most recent backup. On completion, your data will have been restored.

   5. [Reinstall](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/Suite/Licenses_Add.htm) your license file.

   **Important.** After restoring from a backup in a production environment, the **Site type** appears as `Lab` in the Tufin Customer Portal. You must [reinstall](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/latest/Content/Suite/Licenses_Add.htm) the license file; otherwise, TOS deactivates after 30 days. This isn’t required for lab environments.

   </details>

8. <details>
   <summary>Reinstall Tufin Extensions and PS solutions</summary>

   1. Reinstall all extensions. See the [Extensions Knowledge Center](https://forum.tufin.com/support/kc/mkt/parent/Content/Marketplace/home.htm).

   2. Reinstall all Professional Services solutions and reconfigure the cron jobs.

   </details>
